samples.text: For now the period runs on a manual fix. The record states the workaround as manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period, which means valuation has proceeded on hand-entered mappings rather than on the reference data as published. The underlying fault has been identified as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, and the override stands in for that stale entry until the register itself is corrected. That position is provisional and should be read as such. The override was applied to finish the period, not to repair the source, and the stale mapping is still there behind it. Teams deciding whether to wait can rely on the period's valuation as completed under the override. They should not assume the next scheduled run will behave the same way, because the next run will read the register again unless someone has changed it. Anyone who depends on that run should plan for a repeat of the manual step and should expect this note

Confirmed cause: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. The inventory valuation service resolved agency codes through that mapping, and the entries it used no longer matched the codes in force, so the run could not value the records it was given. It was initially recorded as overnight ERP outage, a reading that fitted the overnight timing but had no evidence behind it beyond that. The hypothesis was ruled out on the record: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. One level further down, the classification for the product hierarchy sync service is control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer, which is why a stale entry could sit in the table without anyone noticing.
